FR-001.title: The product MUST make governed portable archives available for Windows on arm64, Windows on amd64, Linux on arm64, Linux on amd64, and macOS on arm64.

FR-002.title: The product MUST document the minimum supported operating-system versions and required system runtime dependencies for each target.

FR-003.title: Every target artifact MUST include the complete Overseer interface, player interface, bundled demo data, product identity, application icon, and required third-party notices.

FR-004.title: A user MUST be able to unpack each target archive and locate its packaged executable and required resources without installing the source repository, a compiler, or frontend build tools.

FR-005.title: This feature MUST preserve existing application behavior without making session, control, player, dialog, lifecycle, or public-access journeys a platform-support or tagged-release acceptance requirement.

FR-006.title: Native UI, dialog, external-link, player, lifecycle, credential-store, tunnel, and signing checks MUST remain optional and non-gating, and unexecuted checks MUST be reported as `NOT RUN` rather than passing evidence.

FR-007.title: Every archive MUST contain only packaged read-only application resources and MUST NOT contain user-owned session documents or private application settings.

FR-008.title: Every archive and automated release output MUST contain zero public-access credentials, plaintext secret fallbacks, or secret-bearing verification records.

FR-009.title: Archive eligibility and platform support MUST NOT require application startup, native interaction, or shutdown evidence.

FR-010.title: Maintainers MUST have a documented packaging command for each supported target that runs on a matching operating-system host without requiring source changes between targets.

FR-011.title: Each produced artifact MUST have a stable, unique name that identifies its operating system and processor architecture.

FR-012.title: The automated delivery workflow MUST define exactly this five-target build matrix from one clean tagged source revision: Windows amd64, Windows arm64, Linux amd64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64.

FR-013.title: Automated per-target archive eligibility validation MUST be limited to successful target compilation, non-empty archive creation, and presence of the executable and required resources; strict native UI, dialog, credential-store, player-journey, signing, and notarization checks MUST NOT gate hobby-project releases.

FR-014.title: A failed or unverifiable target MUST NOT be reported or published as a successful artifact.

FR-015.title: The supported macOS target MUST enter the same explicit target-specific unsigned build-and-portable-archive flow as every Windows and Linux target.

FR-016.title: User-facing documentation MUST explain target selection, prerequisites, launch steps, data locations, credential-service expectations, and platform-specific troubleshooting.

FR-017.title: Documentation and archive diagnostics MUST provide actionable information for platform or architecture mismatches, missing archive contents, and unavailable runtime prerequisites.

FR-018.title: The version-tag workflow MUST withhold GitHub Release publication unless all five required target archives succeed.

FR-019.title: Each target-specific packaging command MUST produce a portable archive containing the target executable and required resources without requiring a native installer.

FR-020.title: The repository MUST migrate its developer, verification, build, package, release, and Spec Kit command aliases from the root Makefile into a root Taskfile compatible with the pinned Wails task-based workflow.

FR-021.title: Go Task MUST be version-pinned in its own isolated Go tool module under `tools/` and MUST be installed through the same repository-owned bootstrap as every other Go development tool.

FR-022.title: The root Makefile MUST retain only one bootstrap responsibility: installing every Go tool declared by the isolated modules under `tools/`, including Go Task; it MAY expose a non-mutating `help` target that points to Task discovery, but MUST NOT remain a parallel owner or proxy of application workflows.

FR-023.title: Existing maintainer workflows currently exposed through Make MUST have documented Task equivalents with preserved ordering, inputs, and failure behavior.

FR-024.title: The accepted Wails Go runtime, isolated CLI tool, and frontend runtime MUST remain pinned exactly to the accepted `v3.0.0-beta.13` / `3.0.0-beta.13` baseline, with committed Go and npm checksums.

FR-029.title: The macOS tagged-release path MUST NOT create or require a DMG, signature, notarization, stapling, or any macOS-specific publication path.

FR-025.title: Every supported target MUST be built from the tagged revision on a compatible runner by invoking the same explicit target-aware repository package entrypoint with that target's operating-system and processor-architecture inputs.

FR-026.title: The release workflow MUST NOT depend on Docker aggregate builds, native UI automation, credential-store integration tests, public-tunnel tests, GitHub Packages publication, signing, notarization, or rollback orchestration.

FR-027.title: Pushing a semantic-version tag in the form vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with an optional prerelease suffix, MUST trigger the complete supported-target build matrix and a single GitHub Release publication flow; other tags, pull requests, and ordinary branch pushes MUST NOT trigger that matrix.

FR-028.title: The GitHub Release MUST contain exactly one uniquely named portable archive per supported target, and each archive MUST contain that target's executable and required runtime resources.

FR-030.title: If a qualifying tag already has a GitHub Release, the workflow MUST fail and MUST leave the existing release and all of its assets unchanged.

FR-031.title: If publication creates a partial GitHub Release and then fails, the workflow MUST leave it unchanged, report instructions for a maintainer to delete it manually, refuse automated reruns while it exists, and allow the same tag to be rerun after its deletion.

FR-032.title: A separate non-release quality workflow MUST run project quality checks for pull requests and pushes to the main branch, MUST NOT run the five-target release matrix, and MUST publish no release assets.

SC-001.title: A successful version-tag run produces exactly five uniquely identified portable archives: Windows amd64, Windows arm64, Linux amd64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64.

SC-002.title: Every published archive is non-empty and contains its target executable plus all required runtime resources.

SC-003.title: Archive inspection for every target requires zero native window, dialog, player, lifecycle, credential-store, tunnel, or signing execution steps.

SC-004.title: Every archive name identifies its operating system and processor architecture with zero collisions across the release.

SC-005.title: Public-access credentials, plaintext secret fallbacks, and secret-bearing verification records are absent from all five archives and every automated release asset.

SC-006.title: Every optional native or external-service check that is unavailable or unexecuted is reported as `NOT RUN` and changes zero archive-eligibility, platform-support, quality-workflow, or tagged-release outcomes.

SC-007.title: A successful macOS target job executes zero signing, notarization, or stapling steps.

SC-008.title: Using only the published guidance, a maintainer can identify the correct artifact, its prerequisites, and its user-data locations for any supported target in under five minutes.

SC-009.title: After one tool-bootstrap command, a maintainer can run every migrated repository workflow through the pinned Task binary, and automated inspection finds no application workflow remaining in the Makefile.

SC-010.title: A controlled target-build failure prevents the tag's release from being published as complete and identifies the failed target.

SC-011.title: A successful version-tag workflow attaches the full supported-target archive set to one GitHub Release without publishing a duplicate raw executable, checksum sidecar, aggregate index, or package-registry copy.

SC-012.title: The release workflow contains zero strict native UI, dialog, secure-store, public-tunnel, signing, notarization, or rollback-orchestration gates.

SC-013.title: The macOS release asset is one non-empty portable archive whose stable name identifies macOS arm64 and whose contents include the packaged application executable and required resources under the same archive eligibility contract as Windows and Linux.

SC-014.title: Re-running publication for a tag that already has a GitHub Release makes zero changes to that release or its assets and reports failure.

SC-015.title: A controlled publication failure after partial release creation performs zero automated deletion or replacement actions, reports the manual deletion-and-rerun procedure, and permits the same tag to publish only after a maintainer deletes the partial release.

SC-016.title: Every pull-request and main-branch quality run publishes zero release assets and invokes zero jobs from the five-target release matrix.

FR-033.title: The repository MUST retain `task package:all` and its Docker implementation as optional maintainer convenience that runs neither in CI nor as a platform-support, quality-workflow, feature-completion, or tagged-release gate.

FR-034.title: The repository MUST remove `package:all:remote`, `release:local`, and their remote aggregation and joined-release implementations, tests, tool dependencies, and active documentation.

FR-035.title: Tagged publication MUST enter through the CI-owned release:publish Task command, which MUST invoke repository-pinned GoReleaser as the sole GitHub Release publisher.

area: operating-system storage, desktop integration, and credential security
area: automated delivery workflow and user documentation
constraint: no local test execution requested
intent: Deliver complete, trustworthy Fallout Terminal desktop distributions for Windows and Linux on arm64 and amd64.
expectations: Local test execution is not required for this specification step.
approach: Define platform support as availability of five governed unsigned portable archives. Keep PR/main quality CI—including Go, Buf/protobuf, frontend, startup, Wails-pin, and binding checks—separate from the SemVer-tag native matrix. Every native target uses the same explicit package entrypoint; CI publication enters through release:publish, which invokes repository-pinned GoReleaser as the sole create-only publisher. Validate statically and locally, including task build and explicit Darwin packaging, then preserve one maintainer-approved live prerelease as acceptance evidence. Retain local Docker package:all outside CI and use conditional manual recovery diagnostics.

decisions.decision: Use matching native OS/architecture runners and task package:all for aggregate orchestration
decisions.why: Native runners satisfy Linux CGO/runtime and real-window evidence while the aggregate command enforces complete-matrix success
decisions.rejected: Local sequential cross-compilation or unrelated manual jobs

decisions.decision: Migrate workflow aliases from Make to a pinned Taskfile while keeping detailed build policy in Go
decisions.why: Wails v3 dispatches build/package through Task and Go retains typed, testable archive and security policy
decisions.rejected: Parallel Make and Task graphs or YAML-only build policy

decisions.decision: Pin github.com/go-task/task/v3/cmd/task v3.53.1 in tools/task and leave Make only as discovery-based all-tool installation
decisions.why: The bootstrap avoids requiring Task to install itself and keeps every Go tool version isolated and complete
decisions.rejected: Global/unpinned Task installation or a hard-coded partial tool list

decisions.decision: Use the pinned Wails default native runtimes: WebView2 and GTK4/WebKitGTK 6.0
decisions.why: These match the accepted runtime and current supported Windows 10/11 and Ubuntu 24.04+/Debian 13+ baselines
decisions.rejected: Legacy GTK3 or bundling platform runtimes

decisions.decision: Use compile-time production identity and executable-relative Windows/Linux resources
decisions.why: This closes the current development-secret override gap and avoids current-working-directory dependence
decisions.rejected: Executable path heuristics or mutable linker/runtime flags

decisions.decision: Resolve writable storage through injectable OS-native directory providers
decisions.why: Windows Known Folders and Linux XDG paths handle redirection and remain testable while preserving macOS locations
decisions.rejected: Hard-coded home-relative or executable-relative writable paths

decisions.decision: Implement native Windows Credential Manager and Linux Secret Service adapters
decisions.why: Direct pinned adapters preserve bounded calls, precise fail-closed errors, and temporary secret clearing
decisions.rejected: Generic string-based keyring wrappers or file/environment fallbacks

decisions.decision: Emit deterministic ZIP/TAR.GZ archives with internal manifests and external SHA-256 sidecars
decisions.why: Stable layouts plus PE/ELF inspection prove target identity, inventory, metadata, and reproducibility before upload
decisions.rejected: Filename-only validation, installers, or committed target-specific generated objects

decisions.decision: Amend the constitution before implementation and preserve macOS as a separate trust path
decisions.why: Current governance both limits deployment to macOS arm64 and prohibits Taskfiles; the authorized feature must update those rules without weakening signed macOS release checks
decisions.rejected: Implementing under standing violations or folding macOS into unsigned portable archives

decisions.decision: Upgrade all active Wails pins together to v3.0.0-beta.13 / 3.0.0-beta.13.
decisions.why: The official Go module proxy and npm registry both list beta.13 as the newest matching published beta on 2026-08-26.
decisions.rejected: Advancing only the Go runtime or only the frontend would violate the repository compatibility pin contract.

decisions.decision: Use one tag-only GitHub Actions workflow with SemVer and existing-release preflight
decisions.why: It prevents invalid or duplicate releases before consuming five native runners and removes PR/main matrix duplication
decisions.rejected: Separate platform workflows and workflow-dispatch release validation

decisions.decision: Build all five targets on matching native runners through task package
decisions.why: The existing Wails build boundary owns frontend, resource, and native host requirements without YAML duplication
decisions.rejected: Cross-compilation or direct go build commands in workflow YAML

decisions.decision: Publish darwin/arm64 as an unsigned portable ZIP containing the application bundle
decisions.why: It preserves required macOS metadata and resources while using the same target-specific archive flow as Windows and Linux
decisions.rejected: Raw Mach-O, DMG, signing, notarization, or darwin/amd64

decisions.decision: Create the GitHub Release directly with GitHub CLI and exactly five archives
decisions.why: One destination and create-only behavior satisfy the hobby-project and immutable-release requirements without extra tooling
decisions.rejected: GoReleaser, third-party release actions, ORAS, GitHub Packages, or rollback orchestration

decisions.decision: Remove superseded aggregate and multi-destination release machinery
decisions.why: No retained workflow consumes it and complete cutover avoids maintaining two release architectures
decisions.rejected: Leaving Docker aggregate, remote dispatch, local release candidate, and retired tools as undocumented legacy

decisions.decision: Separate PR/main quality from tag releases
decisions.why: Broader Go, frontend, startup, Wails pin, and binding checks remain valuable but must not gate hobby releases.
decisions.rejected: Deleting quality CI or running those gates inside the tag workflow.

decisions.decision: Use one explicit package entrypoint on five matching native runners
decisions.why: The existing Go build boundary owns target, frontend, binding, resource, and archive policy.
decisions.rejected: Cross-compilation, raw go build commands, or local Docker release inputs.

decisions.decision: Package darwin/arm64 as an unsigned application-bundle ZIP
decisions.why: ZIP preserves the runnable bundle while matching the common portable archive contract.
decisions.rejected: DMG, raw Mach-O, signing, notarization, stapling, or darwin/amd64.

decisions.decision: Limit tag eligibility to compile, non-empty archive, executable, and resources
decisions.why: This is the approved hobby-project release gate; richer native checks remain optional quality evidence.
decisions.rejected: Checksum-heavy verification or native UI, credential, player, tunnel, and signing gates.

decisions.decision: Keep pinned GoReleaser as the create-only sole publisher
decisions.why: Constitution v7 requires it; two existing-release refusal checks and no replacement option prevent automated reruns from modifying a release.
decisions.rejected: GitHub CLI publication, draft reuse, replacement, or a second publisher.

decisions.decision: Publish exactly five archives to GitHub Releases only
decisions.why: Each archive is the complete user unit and the exact inventory needs no sidecars or aggregate metadata.
decisions.rejected: ORAS, GitHub Packages, checksum assets, indexes, raw executables, DMGs, and multi-destination rollback.

decisions.decision: Use manual recovery for partial GitHub Releases
decisions.why: A maintainer can delete the partial release and rerun the tag without destructive rollback automation.
decisions.rejected: Automatic deletion, append, replacement, or resume.

decisions.decision: Retain local Docker package:all but remove remote and joined-release implementations
decisions.why: The local convenience remains useful and explicitly approved, but it has no CI or tagged-release consumer.
decisions.rejected: Deleting all Docker aggregation or retaining dormant remote orchestration.

decisions.decision: Validate release contracts with static and network-free fixtures
decisions.why: Triggers, inventory, archive presence, config, and recovery can be proven without native dispatch or external publication.
decisions.rejected: workflow_dispatch release rehearsal or live test publication.

decisions.decision: Archive T001-T067 and begin delta tasks at T068
decisions.why: This preserves implemented history while preventing old Companion completion events from checking off new work.
decisions.rejected: Mixing history into the active list, deleting it, or reusing task IDs.

decisions.decision: Define platform support as governed archive availability
decisions.why: Constitution v8 makes executable-and-resource archive production the support boundary while native runtime journeys remain optional and non-gating.
decisions.rejected: Mandatory native launch, UI, dialog, credential-store, player, tunnel, lifecycle, or signing acceptance.

decisions.decision: Keep protobuf governance checks in the separate PR/main quality workflow
decisions.why: Buf formatting, lint, generation drift, breaking checks, and generated-code checks preserve constitution requirements without gating tagged hobby releases.
decisions.rejected: Dropping protobuf checks or moving them into the tag matrix.

decisions.decision: Use repository-pinned GoReleaser as the sole create-only GitHub Release publisher
decisions.why: Two read-only existing-release refusals prevent append or replacement while exactly five prebuilt archives remain the only assets.
decisions.rejected: GitHub CLI publication, draft reuse, asset replacement, append, ORAS, or a second publisher.

decisions.decision: Distinguish publication failure with no release from a partial release
decisions.why: A read-only lookup can tell maintainers to rerun immediately when nothing was created or manually delete then rerun when a partial release exists.
decisions.rejected: Unconditional deletion instructions or automated rollback.

decisions.decision: Relocate every Docker-retained aggregate dependency before deleting the remote coordinator
decisions.why: Optional local package:all must remain functional after aggregate.go and joined-release code are removed.
decisions.rejected: Leaving hidden Docker dependencies in aggregate.go or deleting local Docker convenience.

decisions.decision: Rewrite the portable release workflow before deleting the standalone macOS workflow
decisions.why: The ordered cutover removes the reusable-workflow dependency first and cleans the stale scripts/proto-check.sh reference with deletion.
decisions.rejected: Deleting the macOS workflow before its release caller and quality checks are replaced.

decisions.decision: Treat the Wails beta.13 versions as an exact accepted baseline
decisions.why: The requirement is reproducible pin consistency, independent of whether a newer version is later published.
decisions.rejected: A moving latest-published requirement.

decisions.decision: Constitution v8 supersedes earlier signed-macOS, GitHub CLI, checksum-asset, remote-aggregate, and mandatory-native-evidence choices
decisions.why: The approved hobby-project release design uses five unsigned archives, pinned GoReleaser, local-only Docker convenience, and optional native evidence.
decisions.rejected: Applying superseded constitution v6/v7 planning decisions to the active delta.

decisions.decision: Route tagged publication through the CI-owned release:publish Task command
decisions.why: The workflow remains on the canonical Task graph while repository-pinned GoReleaser stays the sole GitHub Release publisher.
decisions.rejected: Direct GoReleaser invocation from workflow YAML or any second publisher.

decisions.decision: Require task build and explicit darwin/arm64 packaging in local completion validation
decisions.why: These commands exercise the project build and the exact macOS portable package entrypoint before any live tag is approved.
decisions.rejected: Static contract checks as the only pre-publication acceptance evidence.

decisions.decision: Publish and preserve one real prerelease for final tagged-release acceptance
decisions.why: A maintainer-approved unused SemVer prerelease after commit proves the real five-native-target workflow and exact GitHub Release inventory.
decisions.rejected: Static-only acceptance or automated deletion of the successful evidence release.

decisions.decision: Limit FR-013 to per-target archive eligibility
decisions.why: Compilation, non-empty archive creation, executable presence, and resource presence are distinct from SemVer preflight, exact release inventory, and existing-release safety.
decisions.rejected: Using FR-013 to weaken run-level publication and immutability checks.

plan.summary: Constitution v8 plan aligns separate quality CI with a tag-only five-native-target release entered through release:publish and published solely by pinned GoReleaser.
plan.key_finding: Archive availability is the support boundary; final release acceptance adds one preserved maintainer-approved prerelease after static/local validation and commit.
